items.source_quote: September 30 – Animated sitcom The Flintstones airs its first episode on the ABC network in the United States

items.text: Elvis Presley's "It's Now or Never" spent five weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1960.
items.question: Where were you living when Elvis Presley's "It's Now or Never" was on the radio, and who did that song make you think of?
source_quote: The Billboard Hot 100 is a chart published since August 1958 by Billboard magazine which ranks the best-performing singles in the United States. In 1960, it was compiled based on a combination of sales and airplay data sourced from surveys of retail outlets and playlists submitted by radio stations respectively. During the year, 19 different singles spent time at number one.
Presley returned to number one in August with "It's Now or Never", which spent five weeks in the top spot

items.text: Richard Nixon and John F. Kennedy took part in the first televised presidential election debate on September 26, 1960.
items.question: Where did you watch or hear the first Kennedy and Nixon debate, and who was in the room with you?
items.source_quote: September 26 – The two leading U.S. presidential candidates, Richard Nixon and John F. Kennedy, participate in the first televised presidential election debate.

items.text: The Pittsburgh Pirates beat the New York Yankees in the seventh game of the World Series on Bill Mazeroski's walk-off home run.
items.question: Where were you when Bill Mazeroski's home run won the 1960 World Series, and how did you hear about it?
items.source_quote: The Pittsburgh Pirates defeat the New York Yankees in the seventh game of the World Series in baseball on Bill Mazeroski's walk-off home run.
